div.l: His table dormaūnt in his halle alweye
Stode redy coủered all the long daye
At Cessions there was he lord and syre
Full ofte tyme he was knyght of the shire
An anelate and a gysperall of sylk
Hyng at his gyrdell white as morne mylk
A shirreve hadde he been and a countour
Was no wher suche a worthy Vauasour
An haberdassher and a Carpenter
A Webber a dyer and a Tapeser
And they were clothed alle in one lyuerye
Of a soleime and a gret fraternite
Full fressh and newe her ger a pyked was
Her knyves wer chaped nout with bras
But all wᵗith sylủer wrought full clene and weel
Her gyrdelys and her pouches euery deel
Weel semed eche of them a faire burgeys
To sytten̄ in a yelde halle vp on a dees
Eueriche for the wisdome that he can
Was shappely for to been an Alderman̄
For Catell had they y now and rente
And eke her wyves wold it weel assente
And elles certeyn̄ they were to blame
It is full fayr to be cleped Ma dame
And gon to Vigilies all by fore
And haue a mantel ryaliche y bore
A Cook they had with them for the nones
To boyle the checons with the mary bones
And powdre marchaūnt tarte and galynghale
Weel coude he drynk a draught of london ale
He cowde rost and sethe broyle and frye
Maken mortrews and weel baken a pye
But grete wharme wharme harme was it as thout me
That on his shene a mormale had he
For blank manger that made he with the best
A Shipman̄ was ther wonyng fer be west
For out I wote he was of Dertenmowthe
He rood vp on a Rowncy as he cowthe
In a gowne of faldyng to the knee
A dagar hangyng in a lace had hee
A bout his nekke vndre his arme down
That hot somer had made his hew all brown
And certeynly he was a good felawe
Full many draute of wyne had he drawe
From Burdeux Warde wh while þe chapmen slepe
Of nyce concience tok he no kepe
Yf he had fawt and had the heyer honde
By water he sent hem home to eủery londe
But of his craft to rekne weel his tydes
Hise stremes and hise daungers hym by sydes
His herborgh and his moone and his lodemanage
There ne was non suche from hul to Cartage
Hardy he was and wyce to vndertake
With a many a tempeste had his berd ben shake
He knewe alle the havonys as they were
Fro Scotlond to the Cape de Fynestre
And eủery Cryke in Bretayn̄ and in Spayne
His Barge y cleped was the Mawdelayne
With vs ther was a doctour of phisyke
In all the world ne was non hym lyke
To speke of phisyke and of Surgerye
For he was grounded in astronomye
He kept his pacience a full gret dele
In houres by his magyk naturele
Wel coude he fortune the ascendente
Of his ymage for his paciente
He knewe the cause of eủeryche maladye
Wer it of hete or cold or moyst or drye
And where engendred and of what humour
He was a verray parfecte practysour
The cause he knewe and of his harme the rote
A non he gaf the sekeman̄ his bote
Full redy had he his Apotecaryes
To sende hym drugges and electuaryes
For eche of hem made other for to wynne
Her frenship ne was newe for to bygynne
Weel knewe he the olde Escalapius
And Astōmrides and eke Rufus
Olde ypocras haly and Galyen
Serapyoıı̄un Rasy and Aūnyen̄
Aueroys Damascien and constantyne
Bernard and Gatysden and Gilbtyne
Of his diete mesurable was he
For it was of no suꝑperfluite
But of gret noryshyng and digestible
His studye was but litel on the byble
In sangueyne and in pers clad he was all
Lyned wᵗith Tafeta and with sendall
